title: SpaceX weighting in Nasdaq 100 set to more than double - Bloomberg
detail:
SpaceX weighting in Nasdaq 100 set to more than double - Bloomberg
Simon Mugo
Sat, September 12, 2026 at 8:37 PM EDT 2 min read
SPCX
^NDX
QQQ
NDX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- SpaceX is set to receive a significantly larger weighting in the Nasdaq 100 later this month, a change that could trigger billions of dollars in buying from passive funds tracking the index, Bloomberg reported on Saturday.

The rocket and satellite company's weighting is expected to increase to about 2.82% from roughly 1.28%, according to pro forma data from Nasdaq's Global Index Watch circulated late Friday.

The final weighting will be determined later this month. Wall Street expects the adjustment to generate billions of dollars in purchases from index funds and exchange-traded funds that track the Nasdaq 100.

Among the largest vehicles affected is the Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1, which has about $481 billion in assets. Passive funds must adjust their holdings to reflect changes in the composition and weighting of the benchmarks they track.

SpaceX's relatively low weighting dates back to its addition to the Nasdaq 100 in July. At the time, a large portion of the company's shares remained subject to lockup restrictions and could not be publicly traded.

That limited SpaceX's free float and, in turn, the weighting it received in the index. Nasdaq had previously changed its rules to allow newly listed large-cap companies to enter the benchmark sooner and removed a requirement that at least 10% of their shares be publicly tradable.

More SpaceX shares have become available for trading as those lockup restrictions expire, increasing the company's free float and allowing it to command a larger share of the Nasdaq 100.

The adjustment could also increase SpaceX's influence on the performance of the technology-heavy index once the new weighting takes effect.

Further changes are possible. Additional SpaceX shares are scheduled to come out of lockup, potentially increasing its free float and resulting in another rise in the company's index weighting.

SpaceX shares closed at $151.21, up 2.04%, according to Bloomberg data.

Its weighting is expected to rise to about 2.82% from roughly 1.28%, based on pro forma data from Nasdaq's Global Index Watch circulated late Friday. The final weighting will be determined later this month. Wall Street expects the change to result in billions in new buying by index funds and exchange-traded funds that track the benchmark.

SpaceX's relatively small weighting dates to its addition to the gauge in July. Most of its shares were still locked up and unavailable for public trading, limiting the weighting it received even after Nasdaq changed its rules to allow newly listed large-cap companies to enter sooner and eliminated a requirement that at least 10% of their shares be publicly tradable.

As those lockups expire, more SpaceX shares are becoming available for trading. That increases the company's free float, which can, in turn, increase its weighting in the Nasdaq 100.

More adjustments may follow. Additional SpaceX shares are scheduled to come out of lockup, potentially lifting its index weighting again.

SpaceX's first lockup expiration came in August, alongside its first earnings release as a public company, prompting concern that a surge in newly tradable shares could overwhelm demand. The selloff didn't materialize, including after a second lockup expired a week later. Insiders largely held onto their stakes and the stock held up.

The Nasdaq 100 tracks the largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market. There is no minimum market capitalization for inclusion, though companies must have average daily trading volume of at least 200,000 shares and meet other requirements.

A higher weighting matters because passive funds tied to the benchmark must adjust their holdings accordingly. They include the $481 billion Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1, known as QQQ. Roughly $1.7 trillion in assets tracked the Nasdaq 100 as of the end of the second quarter, according to Nasdaq.

US stock futures moved higher on Friday as investors awaited August consumer inflation data ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision next week.

At 02:57 ET (06:57 GMT), Dow futures were up 232 points, or 0.5%, while S&P 500 futures gained 33 points, or 0.4%. Nasdaq 100 futures advanced 120 points, also up 0.4%.

The gains followed another lower session on Wall Street on Thursday, when the S&P 500 declined for a fourth consecutive trading day. Analysts at Deutsche Bank attributed part of the pressure to "another terrible day for bonds."

The US 10-year Treasury yield continued to move towards 5%, while markets assessed the potential inflationary impact of higher oil prices. The European Central Bank also raised interest rates on Thursday, while money markets were pricing in additional increases over the coming year.

"The combination of higher energy prices and a hawkish ECB put fresh pressure on sovereign bonds across the board," Deutsche Bank analysts said.

US CPI Data in Focus Ahead of Fed Decision

Economists expect the US Consumer Price Index to increase 0.4% month on month in August, compared with 0.1% previously, with higher gasoline prices contributing to the expected acceleration.

Annual headline inflation is forecast at 3.4%, unchanged from July.

Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, is expected to increase 0.2% month on month and 2.4% year on year. In July, the respective readings were 0.2% and 2.5%.

The figures will be released ahead of the Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting next week. The source said expectations for a potential rate increase were also supported by Thursday's data showing faster price increases in several components that feed into the personal consumption expenditures price index.

Brent Crude Remains Above $100

Brent crude futures moved lower on Friday but remained above $100 per barrel as markets continued to assess developments affecting Middle East shipping routes.

"Once again, it is geopolitical fears driving everything," Deutsche Bank analysts said.

Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen captured a port city on Thursday, raising concerns about tanker traffic around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.

Vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz fell to seven on Thursday, compared with a 10-day moving average of 15, according to shipping data cited by Reuters.

Brent prices subsequently declined after the Financial Times reported that Gulf foreign ministers and Iranian authorities were seeking a temporary agreement covering shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Earnings Docket: Friday's earnings calendar includes reports from The Kroger Co. (NYSE:KR), Rent the Runway Inc. (NASDAQ:RENT), and Hooker Furnishings Corp. (NASDAQ:HOFT).

The Bull Case and Market Outlook

Despite broader market volatility, fundamental support in the tech and semiconductor sectors remains strong. Market commentator Louis Navellier highlighted that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (NYSE:TSM) reported a 53.3% year-over-year surge in August sales, providing a positive signal for major tech, AI, and data center stocks.

Meanwhile, consumer interest in tech hardware remains active following Apple Inc.'s (NASDAQ:AAPL) product event, where the company unveiled its new folding iPhone Duo alongside strong brand loyalty metrics.

Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Forecast: Rising Yields Test Bulls
Christopher Lewis

^GSPC
NASDAQ 100 Technical Analysis
Daily price chart for NAS100 showing price at 29,583.8, holding above the 50 EMA (29,241.8) and 200 EMA (27,432.8). Source: TradingView

The Nasdaq 100 looks as if it is relatively resilient considering everything that's going on around the world right now, with the Nasdaq 100 trying to rally early in the day.

It'll be interesting to see if there's any type of follow-through as New York comes on. Keep in mind that oil and the inflation risk continue to be a major problem, and the Federal Reserve repricing is out there as well, with the Friday payroll gain of 162,000 versus the roughly 55,000 expected. It has pushed rate hike probabilities toward 60%.

Semiconductors continue to perform well in this index. It looks more or less like sustained upward pressure, but not enough to get overly aggressive.

Dow Jones 30 Technical Analysis
Daily price chart for US30 showing price at 53,034.1 bouncing along the lower boundary of an ascending channel and above the 50 EMA (52,818.8). Source: TradingView

The Dow Jones 30 has shown itself to be somewhat resilient, with the 50-day EMA sitting just below. It's the laggard of the three, though, not by much.

Right now there are some stocks worth watching. Amgen is down 5% pre-market. Novartis reported disappointing clinical trials, and because Amgen has exposure to a competing cardiovascular treatment, it seems like that's coming into the picture as well.

This is estimated to be about 120 points of Dow decline, potentially.

The fundamental backdrop, again, is oil inflation expectations. The 10-year Treasury is hovering right around 4.78%. Energy exposure is benefiting in the Dow, so keep that in mind.

S&P 500 Technical Analysis
Daily price chart for SP500 showing price at 7,710.52, consolidating above the 50 EMA (7,616.19) and 200 EMA (7,211.86). Source: TradingView

The S&P 500 looks like it's trying to turn things around after initially dropping a little bit. Right now, the Brent story and Light Sweet Crude, of course, are both influencing this market.

The most important number might be 4.8% because it seems like when we get above there, it causes a little bit of a negative reaction.

7,800 above is significant resistance. The fulcrum price, if you will, the pivot price, seems to be 7,700, so it's worth watching.

We do have PPI on Thursday and CPI on Friday, and, of course, the Federal Reserve rate decision next week. So, a little bit of choppiness, but it does look like if we can get yields to drop a little bit, the S&P 500 gets a little happier.
